events.title: The death of Pope Pius XII
events.shortBlurb: Eugenio Pacelli, who had guided the Church through world war and defined the Assumption, died at Castel Gandolfo after nineteen years as pope…
body: Eugenio Pacelli was born in Rome on 2 March 1876, and on his sixty-third birthday, 2 March 1939, was elected pope, taking the name Pius XII. Within months Europe was at war, and his pontificate was bound up with the war years: his first encyclical, Summi Pontificatus, and his radio appeal of August 1939 warned of the gathering storm.

His nineteen years saw the definition of the Assumption of Our Lady, proclaimed on 1 November 1950 in the bull Munificentissimus Deus, and a great quickening of the Church's liturgical and scholarly life; his wartime silences and charities alike have been debated ever since.

Stricken by a stroke at his summer residence, he died at Castel Gandolfo in the small hours of 9 October 1958, and was buried in the grottoes of St. Peter's. Nineteen days later the conclave chose the Patriarch of Venice, who took the name John XXIII — and within months astonished the world by summoning a council.
